titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§204–207: Rewards for Münlig, Boorchu, Muqali and Qorchi
part: §§204–207 — Rewards for Münlig, Boorchu, Muqali and Qorchi
about: In the reward-giving after the enthronement of 1206, Chinggis addresses four of his companions in turn. He thanks Münlig for having warned him off a deadly night at his house, seats him with a yearly allowance, and bids his descendants be remembered; he tells Boorchu how, as a youth, Boorchu came to him and stood through a rainy night holding a felt cloak over him, and makes him commander of a ten-thousand on the right wing and free of nine penalties; he gives Muqali the title Guowang and the left-wing ten-thousand; and, remembering Qorchi's old omen, he lets Qorchi choose thirty wives and sets him over the Bargin and the forest peoples.

sentences.t: Tende Čiṅgis Qaγan žarliγ bolžu Müṅlig ečige-de ügülerün:
sentences.l: Then Chinggis Qaγan, decree making, to Münlig father saying:
sentences.i: Then Chinggis Qahan issued a decree, and said to Father Münlig:
sentences.n: Opens the first decree of the part: a converb pair, bolžu (bol- 'become' with žarliγ 'decree', so 'issuing a decree', Ming 做着) and ügülerün 'saying' (-rün, Ming 說). ečige-de is father + dative-locative -de (Ming 行), 'to the father'; the Ming do not translate ečige as a name, and Münlig is addressed as 'father' as an honorific for the elder. The vowel harmony of the case ending: front-vowel stem ečige takes -de, back-vowel stems take -da. The quotation begins at the next word (Shiratori's opening mark is on Törekü-lüġe).

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]
to become, to make (here with žarliγ: 'issue a decree') [做着]

sentences.t: "Törekü-lüġe töreldügsen öškü-lüġe ösülčegsen ölžetü qutuγtu či.
sentences.l: Born-together-with, grown-together-with, fortune-having, blessing-having, you.
sentences.i: “You who were born with us and grew up with us, who have fortune and blessing.
sentences.n: A run of epithets for Münlig, ending in či 'you' (Shiratori's full stop closes it as an address). -lüġe is the comitative 'together with' (Ming 一同) on the stems törekü and öškü, which I take as verbal nouns 'birth' and 'growth' (törekü from töre- 'be born', öškü from ös- 'grow'); töreldügsen and ösülčegsen are reciprocal-collective past participles (-ldü-, -lče- 'together', Ming 共生了的, 共長了的). So the sense is 'one who was born together and grew together with (us)'; the pronoun 'us' is not written. The -tü / -tu possessive 'having' (Ming 有的) in ölžetü and qutuγtu is the recurring pattern: ölže 'felicity' + -tü, qutuγ 'blessing' + -tu. The two are Ming 福有的 and 吉慶有的. Uncertain: that törekü-lüġe really is a verbal noun with the comitative, not a compound.

morph.gloss: birth (verbal noun of töre- 'be born'; uncertain)

sentences.t: Tusa igeġel čin-u kedün ber ažuγ̇u-že.
sentences.l: Help, protecting-aid, your how-many even was.
sentences.i: However much your help and protecting aid has been —
sentences.n: Tusa 'use, benefit' (Ming 恩 here, 'favour') and igeġel 'protecting help' (Ming 護助) are two near-synonyms set side by side. čin-u is 'your' (či + genitive -u on the oblique stem čin-). kedün ber is 'however many' (kedün 'how many', ber 'even, also'). ažuγ̇u-že is a past form of a- 'to be' (Ming 有來) with the emphatic closing particle -že (Ming 也者︀), which Shiratori writes after the full stop of a sentence; the sense is 'there has been'. The sentence is a concessive opener ('however much...') and its main clause comes in the next unit, so my English leaves it hanging with a dash.

morph.gloss: genitive: of (on the oblique stem čin-)

sentences.t: Tere dotora Waṅ-Qān ečige, Seṅgüm anda qojar nama-ji arγadan uriγsan-dur aisurun
sentences.l: That inside Wang-Qan father, Senggum sworn-brother two me-accusative by-trick calling-at, coming-while,
sentences.i: Among those occasions, when Father Wang Qan and Senggum, the two sworn brothers, had called me by a trick, and I was on my way,
sentences.n: The pronoun Tere dotora is 'that interior', 'among those (things)'. Waṅ-Qān ečige 'Wang Qan father' is Shiratori's comma-set apposition with Seṅgüm anda qojar, 'Senggum, sworn brother, the two': 'the two' (qojar) covers both men; anda is the sworn brother (the house rendering). nama-ji is 'me' with the accusative -ji (Ming 行); nama is the oblique stem of bi 'I'. arγadan, 'by a trick' (Ming 智賺着): arγa 'means, trick' with an ending I cannot name for certain (converb -dan?); the sense is clear. uriγsan-dur 'at (the time of) their calling' is a past participle + dative-locative (Ming 喚了時); aisurun is 'coming, as (I) came' (ai- 'come' + -sur-un converb, Ming 來時). The unit breaks a long chain of conditional and converb clauses, whose main verb is büleġei-že three units on.

morph.gloss: Wang Qan, the title of the Kereid ruler (Chinese wang 'prince' with qan) [人名]

sentences.t: žaγ̇ura Müṅlig ečige-jin ger-tür qonoγ̇asu Müṅlig ečige či ese idqaγ̇asu
sentences.l: Road-at Münlig father's house-at, if-stayed-overnight, Münlig father you not if-admonished,
sentences.i: if I had stayed the night on the road at Father Münlig's house, and if you, Father Münlig, had not cautioned me,
sentences.n: A conditional pair: qonoγ̇asu 'if (I) stay the night' (qono- + -γ̇asu, Ming 宿呵) and ese idqaγ̇asu 'if (you) had not cautioned' (ese is the past negative 'not', Ming 不; idqa- Ming 勸當, 'to advise, admonish'; I render 'cautioned' and am not sure the Mongol verb has that exact shape). The ending -γ̇asu 'if, when' (Ming 呵) is the commonest conditional of the book; its front-vowel twin is -ġesü, as in kēġesü below. Münlig is named twice, once in the genitive (ečige-jin, 'of the father', -jin after the long vowel) with ger-tür, 'at the house' (-tür is the back-vowel -dur / -tur form). The apodosis ('I would have been put in boiling water') follows. Note ese, 'not' of a past event, against ülü, which negates the future; compare ülü at §205.

morph.gloss: between, on the road (from žaγ̇ur 'between') [路間]
not (negative of past or perfect events) [不]
to admonish, caution (Ming 勸當; stem uncertain) [勸當呵]

sentences.t: quirun büküi usun-dur hulalun büküi γal- dur oroγdaγ̇ai büleġei-že.
sentences.l: Boiling being water-in, red being fire-in, would-have-been-entered.
sentences.i: I would have been thrown into boiling water, into red fire.
sentences.n: The apodosis, a graphic image in two parallel phrases. quirun (Ming 㳬, a rare character) I read as 'boiling', from the context; the meaning is uncertain. büküi is the participle of bü- 'to be', 'which is'. hulalun is 'red', usun 'water'. Shiratori prints γal- and dur as two words (47–48): γal 'fire' with a stray hyphen, and the dative -dur written apart, and the glossary will keep them as printed. oroγdaγ̇ai is oro- 'enter' + passive -γda- + -γ̇ai, a form Ming 被入 renders 'be entered' and which carries a would-be force ('would have been'); büleġei-že is bü- 'be' in the past, Ming 有來也者. The subject 'I' is understood throughout.

morph.gloss: being, which is (participle of bü-) [有的]
being, which is (participle of bü-) [有的]
dative-locative: at, to, in (printed as a separate word) [裏]

sentences.t: Tere tusa-ji sai sedkižü uruγ-un uruγ-a Kürtele ker umartaγdaqu.
sentences.l: That favour-accusative indeed thinking, descendants' descendants-to until how forgettable.
sentences.i: Thinking of that kindness, how could it be forgotten, down to our descendants' descendants?
sentences.n: sai is the Ming's 纔 'only then, indeed' and I treat it as an emphatic particle after the accusative tusa-ji. sedkižü is sedki- 'to think' + converb -žü, with the front-vowel form -žü (back-vowel -žu); it appears three more times in this part. uruγ-un uruγ-a is 'descendants' + genitive, 'descendants' descendants' / 'to the descendants of descendants', Ming 子孫的 子孫行; the second is the dative-locative -a 'to' (Ming 行), and kürtele is 'until, as far as'. ker umartaγdaqu is 'how (could it) be forgotten?' (umar- 'forget', passive -ta-, future-participle ending -qu, the Ming 可忘了). A rhetorical question, so `i` writes it as one.

sentences.t: Tere tusa sedkižü edöġe saγ̇uri ene nuγ̇u hužaγ̇ur-a saγ̇ulžu hon-dur sara-dur satažu öglige sojurγal čima-da ögsü;
sentences.l: That favour thinking, now seat this corner's root-at having-made-sit, year-in month-in reckoning, ration bounty you-to give-I;
sentences.i: Thinking of that kindness, I have now seated you at the foot of this seat, and, reckoning it by the year and the month, I shall give you rations and bounty.
sentences.n: One converb chain (sedkižü ... saγ̇ulžu ... satažu) ending in ögsü 'I shall give' (ög- + the first-person optative -sü, Ming 與我), which Shiratori closes with a semicolon. Two things are uncertain. First, saγ̇uri ene nuγ̇u hužaγ̇ur-a: Ming 坐次 這隅的 根行 'seat / this / corner's / at the root'; I read 'at the root of this seat's corner', so that Münlig is given a place at the foot of the great seat; nuγ̇u (Ming 隅的) is the doubtful word. Second, satažu 論着 'reckoning, counting', and öglige 'allowance drawn' (Ming 支請), sojurγal 'bounty, favour' (Ming 恩賜) are nouns without an accusative. saγ̇ulžu is saγ̇u- 'sit' + causative -l- + converb, 'having seated', the usual causative of this book (Ming 敎坐着). čima-da is 'to you' (či, oblique čim-, + dative -da, Ming 行).

morph.gloss: corner (uncertain; Ming 隅的 'of the corner') [隅的]
allowance, ration drawn from the store [支請]

sentences.t: maliγ̇an asuγai.
sentences.l: Attendance let-me-pass.
sentences.i: and let me pass my days in attendance on you.
sentences.n: maliγ̇an is the Ming's 侍奉 'attendance, serving' and asuγai 過我 'let me pass' (the first-person optative -γai); I read 'let me spend (my days) in attending (you)', but it is not clear to me who serves whom: the Ming sense might equally be 'let it be passed in service', and I give it with that doubt. Shiratori ends the sentence here with a full stop.

sentences.t: Uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Descendants' descendants-to until, saying, decree it-was-made.
sentences.i: down to their descendants’ descendants.” So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: Closes the speech (Shiratori's closing quote on kürtele"). keġen is the quotative 'saying' (Ming 麽道), the usual frame; žarliγ bolba is 'the decree was made' (bol- 'become', past -ba), the formula that ends every decree of this section. Note that bolba, 'became/was made', has no stated agent: the sense is 'he issued'.

morph.gloss: to become, to be made [做了]

sentences.t: Basa Čiṅgis Qaγan Boγ̇orču-da ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again Chinggis Qaγan to Boγ̇orču saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Boorchu:
sentences.n: Basa 'again' (Ming 再) opens the second decree of the part, the same frame as §204: ügülerün 'saying' (-rün) after the dative. Boγ̇orču-da is Boγ̇orču + dative-locative -da (Ming 行), the back-vowel form after a back-vowel stem, against ečige-de in the first unit. The speech that follows is long and runs to medetügei" at word 280: Shiratori opens it at Üčügen (89), and I mark it with double quotation marks, with single marks inside for the speech of Boorchu that Chinggis quotes.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Üčügen čaγ-tur širγa aγta-tan naiman morid deġermedtežü žaγ̇ura γurban qonožu nekežü aisuqui-dur žolγalduba-že
sentences.l: Small time-at pale gelding-s eight horses having-been-robbed, road-in three having-stayed-nights, pursuing, at-coming we-met.
sentences.i: “When I was small, eight horses, pale geldings among them, were taken from me; I spent three nights on the road, and as I came pursuing, we met.
sentences.n: Chinggis recalls his first meeting with Boorchu. A string of converbs (deġermedtežü, qonožu, nekežü) ends in aisuqui-dur ('at the time of coming': a participle -qui + dative-locative -dur) and the main verb žolγalduba-že, 'we met' (žolγal- 'meet' + reciprocal -ldu- + past -ba, with the closing particle -že; Ming 相遇了). Two doubts. deġermedtežü: Ming 被劫着 'having been robbed', so a passive converb, but I cannot divide it with confidence (deġerme- + a passive suffix + -žü); the later deġermedügsen and deġermedün are the same verb in other forms. And whose horses: the Ming give none; I take them as Chinggis's own. aγta-tan is the plural 'geldings' (aγta + the collective -tan, Ming 等) and morid is mori 'horse' + plural -d (Ming 每). The unit is a converb chain, left whole because the sequence is short; the sentence ends in the speaker's 'we met', not 'you'.

morph.gloss: pale, dun-coloured (Ming 慘白 'pale white') [慘白]
to plunder, rob (Ming 劫) [被劫着]

sentences.t: či. Tende ügülerün: "Muṅtanižu aisuqui nökör-tur nököčeldüšü keġen
sentences.l: You there saying: 'Hardship-suffering comer companion-to let-me-be-companion', saying
sentences.i: You said there, ‘To a companion who has come in hardship, let me be a companion.’
sentences.n: Boorchu's own words as Chinggis remembers them, in single marks (Shiratori's opening mark is on Muṅtanižu). Muṅtanižu is in parentheses in the Ming (艱難着 'being in hardship'): the edition's parentheses mark characters it has supplied, so the word is partly restored, and I read it as a converb of a verb for 'be in hardship'; stem uncertain. aisuqui is the participle 'come' (as before). nökör-tur is nökör 'companion' + dative-locative -tur (Ming 行); nököčeldüšü is the verb from the same root, 'be a companion', with the first-person optative -šü, 'let me' (Ming 做伴我). Compare the optative -sü of ögsü in §204, and -je of nököčeje below. keġen closes the quotation.

sentences.t: ger-tür ečige-dür(i)-jen ber kelen ügeiġü
sentences.l: House-at father-to-own even word without,
sentences.i: without a word, even to your own father at home,
sentences.n: Boorchu left his home without telling even his father: a fragment of one long address to Boorchu that runs on in the next units and ends at nököčežü (143). ečige-dür(i)-jen is ečige + dative-locative -dür, with -(i) and the reflexive-possessive -jen 'one's own' (Ming 自的行). Reflexive endings -ban/-ben/-jen/-jüġen are a recurring pattern: they mean 'his/her/your own', and say whose by the subject, here Boorchu's. ügeiġü is the negative 'without' (ügei 'there is not' + -ġü), Ming 無. The chain has no main verb until nököčežü; I break it here into units of one clause or two and say so on each.

sentences.t: geġü-ben saγ̇an arun nambuγa saγ̇uluγa-ban keġer-e bürküžü
sentences.l: Own-mares milking while-stopped, leather-bag, own leather-pail steppe-in having-covered,
sentences.i: you stopped the milking of your mares, and left your leather bag and pail covered on the steppe,
sentences.n: A second link in the chain: saγ̇an arun is Ming 擠 住時 'milking / while stopped' and I read it as 'while (the milking) was stopped'; the exact form of arun is uncertain. geġü-ben is Ming 騾馬自的行: geġü I take for 'mare' (the Ming say 騾馬, 'mule-horse'), with the reflexive -ben 'own' (Ming 自的行, with accusative force). saγ̇uluγa-ban is saγ̇uluγa 'leather pail' + the same reflexive; nambuγa 'leather bag'. bürküžü is bürkü- 'to cover' + converb -žü, Ming 葢着. Cut at the converb because the next unit changes subject.

sentences.t: min-u oγatur qoṅγor-i talbiγ̇ulžu na-da oroγ šiṅqula-ji unuγ̇ulžu
sentences.l: My bob-tailed liquorice-yellow-accusative having-caused-to-release, to-me black-back white-horse-accusative having-caused-to-ride,
sentences.i: you had my bob-tailed liquorice-yellow horse turned loose, and had me ride your black-backed white horse,
sentences.n: Two causative converbs: talbiγ̇ulžu (talbi- 'release, let go' + causative -γ̇ul-, Ming 敎放了着) and unuγ̇ulžu (uni- 'ride' + -γ̇ul-, Ming 敎騎了着): '(you) having had (it) let loose', 'having made me ride'. The causative suffix is a recurring pattern in this speech. min-u is 'my' (bi, oblique min-, + genitive -u); na-da 'to me' (oblique na-, + dative). qoṅγor is a horse colour, Ming 甘草黄 'liquorice-yellow'; oγatur 'bob-tailed' (Ming 禿尾) and oroγ 'black-backed' (Ming 黑脊) are my readings of the Ming. šiṅqula-ji is the white horse in the accusative (-ji, Ming 行). The sense I give: Boorchu lent Temüjin his own white horse and let the tired one go; the Ming do not say, and the horse could be either man's.

morph.gloss: liquorice-yellow, a horse colour (Ming 甘草黄) [甘草黄馬行]
to release, let go [敎放了着]
dative-locative: at, to, in (on the oblique stem na-)
black back (Ming 黑脊; uncertain) [黑脊]

sentences.t: či öġesün qurdun qubi-ji unužu aduγ̇u-ban ežen ügei talbižu jaγ̇aražu
sentences.l: You yourself swift pale-yellow-accusative having-ridden, own herd owner without having-released, hurrying,
sentences.i: while you yourself rode a swift pale-yellow one, left your own herd ownerless, and hurried,
sentences.n: Continues the chain: unužu is uni- 'ride' + converb -žu (Ming 騎着); talbižu 'having released'; jaγ̇aražu 'hurrying' (Ming 忙着). öġesün is 'oneself' (Ming 自己), emphasising the subject. qubi-ji is a colour of horse (Ming 淡黃 'pale yellow') in the accusative. aduγ̇u-ban is aduγ̇u 'herd (of horses)' + the reflexive -ban. ežen ügei is 'owner (is) not' (ügei 'there is not', Ming 無), so 'ownerless'. Note that Chinggis recalls Boorchu abandoning his own herd to come.

sentences.t: keġer-eče büġed nama-luγ̇a nököčežü
sentences.l: Steppe-from forthwith with-me having-been-companion,
sentences.i: and from the steppe you came at once to be my companion.
sentences.n: The chain's end, nököčežü 'having been a companion' (nököče- 'be a companion' + -žü, Ming 做伴着), with keġer-eče 'from the steppe' (ablative -eče, Ming 自野甸裏) and nama-luγ̇a 'with me' (Ming 與我 一同; the comitative -luγ̇a is the back-vowel twin of -lüġe in the first unit). büġed is Ming 便 'at once, thereupon'. The chain ran from word 110 to here with no main verb; the verb is supplied by the nökör sense, so I close it with a plain 'came to be my companion'.

sentences.t: basa γurban qonoγ nekežü širγa aγta-tan-i deġermedügsen küreġen-dür kürüġesü
sentences.l: Again three nights pursuing, pale gelding-accusative robbed camp-circle-at when-we-arrived,
sentences.i: Again we pursued for three nights, and when we came to the camp where the pale geldings had been taken,
sentences.n: A new episode: basa 'again' (Ming 再). qonoγ is 'night' (Ming 宿) here a bare noun after γurban, 'three nights'. aγta-tan-i: gelding + plural + accusative -i. deġermedügsen is the same verb deġerme- 'plunder' as before, in a past participle (Ming 劫了的 'that had plundered'), qualifying küreġen, the 'circle' (a camp laid out in a ring, Ming 圈子); so 'the camp-circle of those who had plundered'. kürüġesü is kür- 'reach' + the conditional/temporal -ġesü 'when' (Ming 到呵), the front-vowel twin of -γ̇asu. The subject, 'we', is unwritten.

sentences.t: küreġen-ü kižiγ̇ar-a baiqun-i deġermedün hüldežü dutaγ̇ažu abčiraba-že
sentences.l: Camp-circle's edge-at those-standing-accusative robbing, driving, fleeing, brought.
sentences.i: we seized the horses standing at the edge of the camp, drove them off, fled, and brought them back.
sentences.n: The main verb at last: abčiraba-že 'brought' (abči- 'take away' + -ra- + -ba; Ming (將)來了, with the first character in parentheses), after three converbs: deġermedün 'robbing' (-n converb), hüldežü 'driving' (Ming 趕着), dutaγ̇ažu 'fleeing' (迯着). baiqun-i is bai- 'stand' + participle -qun + accusative -i, Ming 立的每行 'those standing'. küreġen-ü is 'of the camp-circle' (genitive -ü), kižiγ̇ar-a 'at the edge' (kižiγ̇ar 'border' + dative -a, Ming 邊行). 'Them' = the horses is my inference; the Ming give only 'those standing'. Cut from the previous unit to keep the chain short.

morph.gloss: to take, bring [(將)來了 也者︀]

sentences.t: bida qojar.
sentences.l: We two.
sentences.i: We two.
sentences.n: A clipped phrase: bida 'we' (the inclusive plural, here Chinggis and Boorchu) with qojar 'two', closed by Shiratori's full stop. It reads as a delayed subject of the unit before ('we two seized...'), but he punctuates it as a sentence, so I keep it apart.

sentences.t: Ečige čin-u Naqu-Bajan ažuγ̇u.
sentences.l: Father your Naqu-Bayan was.
sentences.i: Your father was Naqu-Bayan.
sentences.n: Naqu-Bajan is the name of Boorchu's father; ažuγ̇u 'was' (Ming 有來) is the same past form as in the first unit but without the closing -že. Ečige čin-u is 'your father' (čin-u as before). The point is not stated: the next unit speaks of him as someone Boorchu might have consulted, so I read it as a statement that his father was alive.

sentences.t: Či γaγča köġün in-ü jaγ̇u medežü na-dur nököčekü büleġe.
sentences.l: You only son, his what knowing, to-me being-companion was.
sentences.i: You were his only son, and, whatever you knew of him, you were my companion.
sentences.n: Hard to be sure of. in-ü jaγ̇u medežü: in-ü is 'his' (the oblique stem of ene / tere, 'his'), jaγ̇u 'what' (Ming 甚), medežü 'knowing' (mede- 'know'; Ming 知), so literally 'his what knowing'. I read 'whatever (you) knew of him', which makes the sentence a contrast: Boorchu, an only son, with a father to consider, still chose to be a companion; but jaγ̇u might also be the indefinite 'anything', giving 'knowing nothing of his (will)'. na-dur is 'to me' (dative-locative on na-); nököčekü büleġe is a participle + 'was', 'was a companion', a periphrastic past (Ming 做伴 有來). Capitalised Či here begins a new sentence.

sentences.t: Sedkil-ün külüg(i)-jer nököčebe-že
sentences.l: Heart's hero-with was-companion.
sentences.i: You were my companion, a hero of the heart.
sentences.n: sedkil-ün külüg(i)-jer is 'with the heart's hero' (sedkil 'heart', genitive -ün, külüg 'hero' + instrumental -jer; Ming 心的 豪傑 敎): the instrumental sense is 'as a hero of the heart', or 'with a hero of the heart'. The Ming 敎 (causative) hints that Chinggis is saying he was given such a companion; the subject is not written, and I take 'you' from the surrounding address. nököčebe-že is 'was a companion' (-be past, with -že). Uncertain case: -jer may be Ming's 敎 'cause'.

morph.gloss: to be a companion [做伴了 也者︀]

sentences.t: či. Teġün-ü qoina sedkižü jabužu bi Belgütei-ji iležü nököčeje kēġesü
sentences.l: You that's after thinking going, I Belgütei-accusative having-sent, 'let-us-be-companions' when-I-said,
sentences.i: After that, as you were thinking it over and setting out, I sent Belgütei, and when I said, 'Let us be companions,'
sentences.n: Another converb chain, cut where the verb of speech ends it. teġün-ü qoina is 'after that' (teġün-ü, genitive of the demonstrative; qoina 'behind, after', Ming 後). sedkižü 'thinking'; jabužu 'going' (Ming 行着). Belgütei-ji is accusative (Ming 行), iležü 'sending' (ile- + -žü, Ming 敎去着). nököčeje is the first-person plural optative of nököče-, 'let us be companions' (-je, Ming 咱); kēġesü is 'when (I) said' (ke- + -ġesü; long ē is Shiratori's), the same conditional as kürüġesü. The syntax is loose: it is not clear whether you or I sent whom; the Ming 敎去着 'having caused to go' fits Chinggis as sender.

morph.gloss: to be a companion [做伴 咱]

sentences.t: či bökötür qoṅγor-i unužu boro örmege-ben bögtürčü nököčen ireġesü
sentences.l: You hump-backed liquorice-yellow-accusative having-ridden, blue felt-coat-own having-carried-on-back companion when-came,
sentences.i: you rode your humpbacked liquorice-yellow horse, carried your blue felt cloak on your back, and came as a companion;
sentences.n: bökötür 'humpbacked' (Ming 拱脊) and boro 'blue-grey' (Ming 靑; the same word as in Börte Čino) are my readings. örmege-ben is örmege 'felt cloak' + reflexive -ben ('your own'; Ming 氁衫 自的行); bögtürčü is 'carrying on the back' (Ming 䭾着). nököčen 'as a companion' is a -n converb; ireġesü 'when (you) came' (ire- + -ġesü). The -ġesü clause waits for its main verb, which comes in the next unit (qučilduba-že).

morph.gloss: carrying on the back (Ming 䭾着; stem uncertain) [䭾着]

sentences.t: γurban Merkid bidan-dur irežü Burqan-(n)i γurbanta qučiγ̇ulqui-dur qučilduba-že
sentences.l: Three Merkid to-us having-come, Burqan-accusative three-times at-causing-to-circle, we-were-encircled-together.
sentences.i: the three Merkid came upon us, and when they made us circle Burqan three times, we circled it together.
sentences.n: The close of the Merkid story. γurban Merkid, 'the three Merkid' (house form; the Ming 種名 only say it is a people), bidan-dur 'to us' (bida 'we' with the oblique -n-, + dative-locative); irežü 'having come'. Burqan-(n)i is the mountain in the accusative (-(n)i, Ming 行), γurbanta 'three times'; qučiγ̇ulqui-dur is the causative qučiγ̇ul- 'make circle' (Ming 敎繞) + participle + dative-locative, 'at the time of making (us) circle', and qučilduba-že the reciprocal 'we circled together' (qučil- 'circle', -ldu-). Subject of the causative: the Merkid, so the passive-ish 'they made us circle'.

morph.gloss: the Merkid, a people (Ming 種名) [種名]
dative-locative: at, to, in (on the oblique stem bidan-)
to circle, go around [敎繞 時]
to circle, go around [共繞了 也]

sentences.t: či. Basa teġün-ü qoina Tatar irgen-dür Dalan-Nemürges-te šitüġeġeldüžü qonoγ̇asu
sentences.l: You. Again that's after Tatar people-at Dalan-Nemürges-in having-mutually-resisted, when-we-stayed-the-night,
sentences.i: You, again after that: when we lay camped at Dalan-Nemürges, face to face with the Tatar people,
sentences.n: Či closes the thought before (Shiratori's full stop is on či.), so it is the vocative 'you' opening a new sentence about Boorchu. Tatar irgen-dür: dative-locative on 'people' (irgen), Ming 百姓行, here 'against / facing'. Dalan-Nemürges-te is a place name with the locative -te (front-vowel twin of -ta; the Ming give 行 as for the dative). šitüġeġeldüžü is a reciprocal (-ldü-) converb of a verb for 'resist' (Ming 共抗拒着); the stem is uncertain. qonoγ̇asu is 'if/when (we) stayed the night' (qono- + -γ̇asu, as in §204).

morph.gloss: the Tatars, a people (Ming 種名) [種名]
to resist, withstand (stem uncertain) [共抗拒着]

sentences.t: qura üdür süni ürgülži žüsereküi-dür süni nama-ji norγ̇atuγai keġen
sentences.l: Rain day night continually, in-pouring-time night me-accusative let-sleep, saying
sentences.i: Rain fell day and night without a break, and when it poured at night he said that I should be allowed to sleep, and
sentences.n: The rain came 'by day, by night, continually': qura 'rain', üdür 'day', süni 'night', ürgülži 'always, continually' (Ming 如常). žüsereküi-dür is a participle of a verb 'to pour (rain)' (Ming 霖雨下) + dative-locative, 'when it poured'. norγ̇atuγai is Ming 睡敎得者 'let (someone) be made to sleep', an imperative in -tuγai (third person 'let him') with a causative sense; nama-ji is 'me' accusative. I read it as Boorchu's wish that Chinggis ('me', in Chinggis's own telling) be allowed to sleep, and keġen 'saying' closes it; so `i` reports it indirectly rather than in marks, since the 'me' is Chinggis's and not Boorchu's. Doubtful: the exact causative sense of norγ̇atuγai. The subject, Boorchu, is not written; `i` supplies 'he'.

morph.gloss: to pour (of rain; stem uncertain) [霖雨下 時]
to sleep, lie down (stem uncertain) [睡敎得者︀]

sentences.t: nemürge-ben nemürügseġer min-u deġere qura ülü čuburiγ̇ulun
sentences.l: Own felt-cloak felt-cloaked, my above rain not letting-leak,
sentences.i: he wrapped himself in his felt cloak and stood over me, not letting the rain leak through on me,
sentences.n: nemürge-ben is nemürge 'felt cloak' + reflexive -ben (Ming 氈衫 自的行); nemürügseġer is 'wearing the felt cloak' (a converb from the same noun, Ming 氈衫披着). min-u deġere is 'my above', i.e. 'over me' (deġere 'above, on', Ming 上). qura ülü čuburiγ̇ulun is 'not letting the rain leak' (čubur- 'leak' + causative -γ̇ul- + converb -n; Ming 敎漏): ülü is the negative that goes with converbs and future forms, against ese, which negates a past event; both are Ming 不. The 'he' is Boorchu, in keeping with 'saying' before; the Mongol only has the converbs.

morph.gloss: to wear a felt cloak (from nemürge; uncertain) [氈衫披着]
not (negative before converbs and the future) [不]

sentences.t: süni daγ̇ustala baižu öreġele köl(i)-jen γaγčanda jeġüdgežü büleġe
sentences.l: Night until-it-finished standing, one leg own singly changing was.
sentences.i: he stood until the night was ended, changing from one leg to the other, a single one at a time.
sentences.n: daγ̇ustala is daγ̇us- 'be finished' + -tala 'until' (Ming 盡了直到); baižu 'standing' (Ming 立着). öreġele (Ming 隻 'single') and köl(i)-jen 'one's own leg(s)' (köl 'foot', reflexive -jen; Ming 腳自的行) with γaγčanda 'singly, one at a time' (Ming 獨次) and jeġüdgežü 'changing' (Ming 換着), then büleġe 'was' (Ming 有來). Shiratori prints no pause after jeġüdgežü; the picture is of a man alternating on his legs through the night. öreġele is uncertain.

morph.gloss: to be finished, to end [盡了直到]

sentences.t: či. Külüg-ün čin-u belge ažuγ̇u-že.
sentences.l: You. Hero's your sign was.
sentences.i: This was the sign of the hero in you.
sentences.n: Či. is the vocative that begins the sentence: 'you'. külüg-ün čin-u belge is 'a hero's, your sign' (külüg 'hero' + genitive -ün; čin-u 'your'; belge 'sign, token', Ming 效驗 'proof'), ažuγ̇u-že 'there was' (Ming 有來也者, as in the first unit). The Ming word order 'hero's, your sign' means 'your sign of being a hero', which I read as 'the sign of the hero in you'.

sentences.t: Teġün-eče busu ali külüg-i čin-u ügüležü daγ̇usqu.
sentences.l: That-than other what hero-accusative your speaking will-be-finished?
sentences.i: What other hero is there whom you could speak of to the end, besides him?
sentences.n: Teġün-eče busu is 'other than that' (ablative -eče 'than', Ming 那箇行, busu 'other'). ali külüg-i is 'which hero (accusative)'; čin-u ügüležü is 'your speaking' (ügüle- + converb); daγ̇usqu is a future participle of daγ̇us- 'be finished', 'will be finished' (Ming 盡的). A rhetorical question, so that `i` writes it as one: after the praise in the previous unit Chinggis asks what more could be said. The grammar is clipped, and the Ming 'other / which hero / your speaking / finishing' leaves the subject unsure: it could also be 'what other hero would you finish naming?' I give the first.

morph.gloss: to be finished, to be exhausted [盡的]

sentences.t: Boγ̇orču, Muqali qojar žöb min-u jabutala žigtüžü
sentences.l: Boorchu, Muqali two right, my until-going having-dragged,
sentences.i: You two, Boorchu and Muqali, who were in the right, dragged me along as I went,
sentences.n: Boγ̇orču, Muqali qojar is 'Boorchu, Muqali, the two' (Ming 兩箇); žöb is 'right, correct' (Ming 是的). jabutala is jabu- 'go' + -tala 'until', min-u jabutala 'until my going / until I went'; žigtüžü 'dragging' (Ming 拽着). Bound by the next unit: the two verbs are a pair (dragging me while I walked, holding me when I stood), a man 'in the wrong' being the speaker. So the speech turns to addressing both Boorchu and Muqali at once. Shiratori puts a comma after Boγ̇orču.

sentences.t: buruγ̇u-ji min-u baitala idγažu ene oron-dur kürgebe.
sentences.l: Wrong-accusative my until-standing-upright having-checked, this seat-at brought.
sentences.i: and when I was in the wrong held me back until I stood upright, and brought me to this seat.
sentences.n: buruγ̇u-ji is buruγ̇u 'wrong, mistaken' (Ming 不是的) in the accusative: 'the one in error (me)'; min-u baitala is 'until my standing' (bai- 'stand' + -tala, Ming 直立了), idγažu 'checking, holding back' (idγa- 'restrain', Ming 止當着; a different idqa- from §204's idqaγ̇asu 'admonished', though both have Ming 當). ene oron-dur is 'at this place / throne' (oron 'place, seat' + -dur, Ming 位裏); kürgebe is kür-ge- 'cause to reach, bring' + -be, Ming 到了. No object ('me') or subject ('you two') is written. Doubtful which of 'the wrong' and 'my standing' the Ming are glossing, as the structure repeats in the pair.

morph.gloss: to restrain, hold back (stem uncertain) [止當着]

sentences.t: Edöġe bürin-ü deġere saγ̇uri saγ̇užu jesün aldal- dur bu aldatuγai.
sentences.l: Now all's above seat having-sat, nine fault-at not let-be-penalised.
sentences.i: Now let him sit in a seat above all the rest, and let him not be punished for nine offences.
sentences.n: Edöġe 'now' (Ming 如今). bürin-ü deġere is 'all's above', i.e. 'above everyone' (bürin 'all', genitive; Ming 衆的上). saγ̇uri saγ̇užu is 'having sat in the seat'. jesün aldal-dur: 'nine' (Ming 九次 'nine times'), aldal 'fault, penalty' (Ming 罰) with the dative -dur printed as a separate word, as at γal- dur. bu aldatuγai is 'let him not be penalised' (bu is the prohibitive 'not', Ming 休; aldat- the passive of alda- 'err, be at fault', with the third-person imperative -tuγai; Ming 罰者). Boorchu is named in the next unit; I supply 'he' as the subject. The nine offences is a privilege, the rule in later sources, but the Ming say only 'nine'.

morph.gloss: dative-locative: at, to, in (printed as a separate word) [裏]
to err, be at fault [罰者︀]

sentences.t: Boγ̇orču baraγ̇un γar-un Altai derelekün-ü tümen medetügei" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Boorchu right-hand Altai pillowing ten-thousand let-him-govern, saying, decree it-was-made.
sentences.i: Let Boorchu govern the ten-thousand lying on the Altai at the right hand.” So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: Boorchu's reward: the command of a tümen, a ten-thousand, on the right (western) wing. baraγ̇un γar-un is 'of the right hand' (baraγ̇un 'right', γar 'hand', genitive -un; Ming 右手的); Altai is the mountain; derelekün-ü is the participle derele- 'pillow, lie on' (Ming 枕的), genitive: 'of the (one) pillowed on', so a tümen whose position is 'pillowed' on the Altai (Ming 枕的萬戶). medetügei is mede- 'know, administer' + third-person imperative -tügei (Ming 敎管者, 'let him manage'), the front-vowel twin of -tuγai. The speech's closing mark is on medetügei", and keġen žarliγ bolba ends the decree as at the end of §204.

morph.gloss: to pillow, to rest on (uncertain) [枕的]
ten-thousand, a division of ten thousand [萬戶]
to become, to be made [做了]

sentences.t: Basa Muqali-da Čiṅgis Qaγan ügülerün:
sentences.l: Again to Muqali Chinggis Qaγan saying:
sentences.i: Again Chinggis Qahan said to Muqali:
sentences.n: The frame again: basa, a dative-locative (Muqali-da, Ming 行), ügülerün 'saying'. Chinggis's speech begins at Bida (289) and runs, in Shiratori's marks, to medetügei" at 334, but it breaks in the middle (word 324, Γuowaṅ nere ögbe, is narration); I therefore close the first speech at keġen (323) and reopen at 327, and say so on those units.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Bida Qorqonaγ-Žubur-un Qutula Qān-(n)u desekü saγlar modun-a baγ̇uγ̇asu
sentences.l: We Qorqonaq-Jubur's Qutula Qan's rejoicing bushy tree-to when-we-alighted,
sentences.i: “When we alighted at the bushy tree of Qorqonaq-Jubur, where Qutula Qan rejoiced,
sentences.n: bida 'we' (inclusive) opens the speech. The place is Qorqonaγ-Žubur-un (Ming 地名的, genitive) and the person Qutula Qān-(n)u (genitive -(n)u, Ming 皇帝的); desekü is a participle of dese- (Ming 喜躍 'leaping for joy'), and the whole phrase qualifies the tree: saγlar modun-a is 'to the bushy / thick-leaved tree' (Ming 鬅鬆木行, 'dishevelled tree'; saγlar 'bushy' is my reading, with modun 'tree' + dative -a). baγ̇uγ̇asu is baγ̇u- 'alight, dismount' + the conditional/temporal -γ̇asu (Ming 下呵), 'when we alighted'. The house form for the title is Qān in the short form 'Qan', Qaγan 'Qahan'; here Qutula is a Qan, Opens a long chain, cut in three.

morph.gloss: qan, ruler (the short title Qan) [皇帝]
to leap for joy, rejoice (stem uncertain) [喜躍的]

sentences.t: Muqali-da teṅgeri-jin žaγ̇arin žaγ̇aγsan üge temdeg-ün tula
sentences.l: Muqali-to Heaven's divine-telling having-told word sign's on-account,
sentences.i: because of the plain sign in the word that Heaven's revelation spoke to Muqali,
sentences.n: Muqali-da: dative 'to Muqali' (Ming 行). teṅgeri-jin is 'Heaven's' (teṅgeri + genitive -jin; Ming 天的), žaγ̇arin 'divine telling, revelation' (Ming 神吿), žaγ̇aγsan 'having told' (Ming 吿了的): Heaven's revelation 'told' a word to Muqali. temdeg-ün tula: 'on account of the sign' (temdeg 'sign, mark', Ming 明白 'plain, clear'; tula 'for the sake of, on account of', Ming 上頭). The sign is the plain meaning of the word revealed. This is the grounds for the next unit's main clause, which has the verb of thinking.

morph.gloss: divine telling, revelation (Ming 神吿) [神︀吿]
on account of, for the sake of [上頭]

sentences.t: bi tende Küġün-Γoγ̇a-ji sedkižü Muqali-da üge baraluγ̇a.
sentences.l: I there Küyün-Goa-accusative thinking, to-Muqali word was-finished.
sentences.i: I thought there of Küyün-Goa, and the word to Muqali was fulfilled.
sentences.n: Küġün-Γoγ̇a-ji is the name of a person (Ming 人名行) in the accusative -ji, object of sedkižü 'thinking' (as in §204: sedki- + -žü): 'I thought of Küyün-Goa'. What follows is Muqali-da üge baraluγ̇a: üge 'word', baraluγ̇a 'was finished, came to an end' (bara- 'be used up, finished' + a past ending; Ming 了了來), which I render 'was fulfilled', taking 'finished' of a prophecy. This is my guess, and the Ming (who gloss only 'the word was finished') do not support it more strongly. I cannot say who Küyün-Goa is from the Ming; the unit's only point is that Chinggis thought of that person and the word given to Muqali had come to its end.

morph.gloss: to be used up, to end (uncertain) [了了來]

sentences.t: Teġü-ber saγ̇uri deġere saγ̇užu
sentences.l: For-that-reason seat above having-sat,
sentences.i: For that reason he is to sit in a seat above the others,
sentences.n: Teġü-ber is 'by that / for that reason' (the demonstrative teġü + instrumental -ber, Ming 爲那般). saγ̇uri deġere saγ̇užu 'having sat on the seat', exactly as in §205. Chinggis is about to decree a title for Muqali's line. This begins the second half of the speech; I add 'he is to' because the next unit's imperative boltuγai needs its subject; the Mongol names no one.

sentences.t: Muqali-jin uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele gür irgen-ü γuowaṅ boltuγai keġen
sentences.l: Muqali's descendants' descendants until, all the people's Guowang let-be, saying
sentences.i: and Muqali's descendants, down to their descendants' descendants, are to be Guowang of all the people.”
sentences.n: Muqali-jin is 'of Muqali' (genitive -jin after a vowel stem, as in teṅgeri-jin). Uruγ-un uruγ-a kürtele 'down to descendants' descendants' as in §204. gür irgen-ü is 'of all the people' (gür 'whole, all', Ming 普, with irgen 'people' in the genitive, Ming 百姓的). γuowaṅ (lower case in Shiratori; Ming 國王, 官名) is the Chinese title guowang. boltuγai is bol- 'become' + third-person imperative -tuγai ('let it be'), Ming 敎做者︀; keġen 'saying'. Shiratori prints no closing quotation mark here; I close it in `i` because the next unit is narration.

morph.gloss: Guowang, the Chinese title 國王 'prince of the state' (written in its own characters) [(官名)]

sentences.t: Γuowaṅ nere ögbe.
sentences.l: Guowang name he-gave.
sentences.i: He gave him the title of Guowang.
sentences.n: Narration, a short clause: Γuowaṅ is again the Chinese title (Ming 國王, capitalised here), nere 'name, title, rank' (Ming 名分, 'rank'), ögbe 'gave' (ög- + -be; Ming (與了) in parentheses, a restored gloss). The Mongol names neither giver nor receiver; the sense is that Chinggis gave Muqali the title. Compare the same sentence in §202.

morph.gloss: Guowang, the Chinese title 國王 'prince of the state' (written in its own characters) [(官名)]

sentences.t: Muqali Γuowaṅ žeġün γar-un Qaraγ̇un-Židun-i derelekün-ü tümen medetügei" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Muqali Guowang left hand's Qaraqun-Jidun-accusative pillowing ten-thousand let-him-govern, saying, decree it-was-made.
sentences.i: “Let Muqali, Guowang, govern the ten-thousand lying on Mount Qaraqun-Jidun at the left hand.” So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: The grant to Muqali, matching Boorchu's at the right hand (§205). žeġün γar-un is 'of the left hand' (žeġün 'left'; Ming 左手的); Qaraγ̇un-Židun-i is the mountain in the accusative (Ming 山名行), the thing 'pillowed upon' (derelekün-ü, as at §205). The rest is as before: medetügei, keġen, žarliγ bolba. Shiratori prints a closing quotation mark at medetügei" but no opening mark; I supply the opening one at Muqali in `i`, since this is a fresh decree. The Chinese title is repeated before the name (Γuowaṅ), now in apposition: 'Muqali the Guowang'.

morph.gloss: Guowang, the Chinese title 國王 'prince of the state' (written in its own characters) [(官名)]
to pillow, to rest on (uncertain) [枕的]
ten-thousand, a division of ten thousand [萬戶]
to become, to be made [做了]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan Qorči-da ügülerün:
sentences.l: Chinggis Qaγan to Qorchi saying:
sentences.i: Chinggis Qahan said to Qorchi:
sentences.n: The same frame as before: ügülerün 'saying' (here unprefixed by basa, the first decree of the section). Qorči-da: dative -da on the name (Ming 人名行). Qorchi is the seer whose omen the speech recalls. The speech runs from Žüṅležü (342) to ab" at 388.

morph.gloss: Chinggis, the title borne by Temüjin from 1206 [太祖︀]

sentences.t: "Žüṅležü nama-ji üčügen büküi-eče
sentences.l: Having-foretold me small from-being,
sentences.i: “You foretold things for me, from the time I was small,
sentences.n: Žüṅležü is Ming 先兆着 'foreboding': an omen, a portent (žüṅ 'omen', Ming 先兆), with a verbal suffix and the converb -žü; 'having given omens'. nama-ji is 'me' accusative. üčügen büküi-eče is 'from (when I) was small' (üčügen 'small', büküi the participle 'being', ablative -eče; Ming 小有行). The 'you' (Qorchi) is not written; I supply it from the addressee. The chain is long, with a sequence of ablative, adverbs and four converbs; I break it here and again at the verb jabuba-že.

morph.gloss: to give an omen, to foretell (from žüṅ 'omen') [先兆着]

sentences.t: ežiġe tuluγ noitan nošildužu köiten köšildüžü nendü qutuγ bolžu jabuba-že
sentences.l: To-now long wet having-been-wet-together, cold having-been-cold-together, fortune blessing having-become, went.
sentences.i: and down to this day you went with me through long wet and cold, to be my fortune and blessing.
sentences.n: ežiġe 'to now' (Ming 到今) and tuluγ (Ming 久遠, 'a long time'); noitan and köiten are 'wet' and 'cold' with the reciprocal converbs nošildužu and köšildüžü ('being wet / cold together', Ming 共濕着, 共寒着; the Ming write köiten 地名, 'place name', which cannot be right here, so I take it as 'cold' from its pair and the converb). nendü qutuγ bolžu is Ming 福 神 做着: nendü 'good fortune' and qutuγ 'blessing', 'becoming (my) fortune and blessing'. jabuba-že 'went' (jabu- + -ba + -že). 'With me' is my addition; the Mongol has none, the object of nama-ji being earlier. Doubt: tuluγ and nendü.

morph.gloss: until now, to this day [到今]
to be wet (from noitan; uncertain) [共濕着]
cold (the Ming gloss, 地名 'place name', seems a slip) [地名]
to be cold (from köiten; uncertain) [共寒着]
to go, to travel [行了 也者︀]

sentences.t: či. Qorči tere čaγ-tur ügülerün:
sentences.l: You, Qorchi, that time-at saying:
sentences.i: You, Qorchi, said at that time:
sentences.n: Či. 'you' followed by Shiratori's full stop, and a new sentence. tere čaγ-tur is 'at that time' (čaγ 'time' + dative -tur; Ming 那時裏). The inner speech opens at Žüṅ (361) and closes at keġeleġe; I mark it with single marks inside the double.

sentences.t: "Žüṅ žöb boluγ̇asu teṅgeri-de sedkil-dür kürgegdeġešü nama γučin emestü bolγa keġeleġe
sentences.l: Omen true if-it-be, Heaven-to heart-at if-conveyed, me thirty wife-having make, you-said.
sentences.i: ‘If the omen is true, and is carried to the heart of Heaven, make me one who has thirty wives,’ you said.
sentences.n: Qorchi's wish, inside Chinggis's speech. žüṅ žöb boluγ̇asu is 'if the omen is right / becomes true' (žöb 'right', Ming 是; boluγ̇asu 'if (it) becomes', bol- + -γ̇asu 'if', Ming 做呵). teṅgeri-de sedkil-dür kürgegdeġešü is 'if (it) is conveyed to Heaven, to (its) heart': two datives (-de, -dür; Ming 天行 心裏) and the passive conditional kürgegdeġešü (kür- 'reach', -ge- causative, -gde- passive, Ming 被到呵) — a long form and the shape of its ending is not clear to me. nama γučin emestü bolγa: 'me thirty wife-having make' (emestü is emes 'wives' + possessive -tü, Ming 妻有的, the possessive 'having'; bolγa 'make' is bol- + causative -γa, Ming 敎做). keġeleġe 'you said' (ke- + past, Ming 說來). The 'you' is not written; I take it from the preceding unit.

sentences.t: či. Edöġe žöb tula sojurγažu
sentences.l: You. Now right on-account, having-bestowed-favour,
sentences.i: Now, because it is right, I bestow a favour on you:
sentences.n: Či. is again a vocative opening the new sentence. edöġe 'now', žöb tula is 'because (it is) right / true' (tula 'on account of', Ming 上頭), sojurγažu 'bestowing favour' (sojurγa- 'to favour, grant'; Ming 恩賜着), the converb of the noun-verb sojurγal seen in §204. The argument of the favour comes in the next unit, which has the imperative; the 'I' is not written but is Chinggis.

morph.gloss: on account of, for the sake of [上頭]
to favour, to bestow (Ming 恩賜) [恩賜着]

sentences.t: ede oroγsad irgen-ü sain eme-ji sain öki üžežü γučin emes soγ̇oṅγužü ab" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: These having-entered people's good woman-accusative good girl having-looked, thirty wives having-chosen take, saying, decree it-was-made.
sentences.i: Among these peoples who have come in to us, look over the good women and good girls, choose thirty wives, and take them.” So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: oroγsad is Ming 投入的每 'those who have come over, submitted' (oro- 'enter' + -γsad, the plural past participle), qualifying irgen-ü 'of the people' (genitive); ede 'these' (Ming 這的每). sain eme-ji sain öki is 'good woman (accusative), good girl'; üžežü 'looking' (üje- 'see', Ming 看着); emes 'wives' (plural of eme); soγ̇oṅγužü 'choosing' (Ming 選揀着); ab is the bare-stem imperative 'take' (Ming 要; the stem ab- 'take'). Shiratori closes the speech with ab". keġen žarliγ bolba as before. The rule: the omen of Qorchi has come true and Chinggis fulfils it from the newly submitted peoples.

morph.gloss: to enter, to come over [投入的每]
to choose, to pick out (stem uncertain) [選揀着]
to become, to be made [做了]

sentences.t: Basa "Qorči γurban miṅγad Baγ̇arin-u deġere
sentences.l: Again Qorchi three thousand Bargin's over,
sentences.i: “Again: Qorchi is to command the three thousand Bargin,
sentences.n: Basa and the speech opens again at Qorči (a double mark, Shiratori's). γurban miṅγad is 'three thousands' (miṅγad, plural of miṅγan 'thousand', Ming 千每); Baγ̇arin-u deġere is 'of the Bargin, over' (genitive; Ming 種名的上), a people, with deġere 'over, above' (as in 'seat above all'). The head of the sentence is slow to come: the verb is medežü (408), 'administering', and the imperative medetügei (423). I break this long period into four units.

morph.gloss: the Bargin, a people (Ming 種名) [種名 的]

sentences.t: Taγai, Ašiγ qojar-luγ̇a Adarkin-u Činos, Töġöres, Teleṅgüd bolun tüme düġürčü
sentences.l: Taqai, Ashiq two-with Adarkin's Chinos, Tögöres, Telengüt becoming ten-thousand having-filled,
sentences.i: together with Taqai and Ashiq, and with the Chinos, Tögöres and Telengüt of the Adarkin, filling up the ten-thousand,
sentences.n: Two names in apposition, then the people: Taγai and Ašiγ are men (Ming 人名), qojar-luγ̇a 'with the two' (comitative -luγ̇a, Ming 兩箇一同); Adarkin-u is 'of the Adarkin' (a people, genitive) governing the three clan names Činos, Töġöres, Teleṅgüd (Ming 種名 each). bolun is bol- 'become' + converb -n, Ming 共做 'making together'; tüme is the ten-thousand (tümen without its final -n, Ming 萬), düġürčü 'having filled' (Ming 滿着). The sense of the unit is that these groups together make up the full tümen. The word-order is flat; the 'Adarkin's Činos, Töġöres, Teleṅgüd' might equally be three peoples in list, the Ming only say 種名 for each.

morph.gloss: the Adarkin, a people (Ming 種名) [種名的]
the Činos, a clan (Ming 種名) [種名]
the Töġöres, a clan (Ming 種名) [種名]
the Telengüt, a people (Ming 種名) [種名]
to be full, to fill (stem uncertain) [滿着]

sentences.t: Qorči medežü Erdis-i γudus hoi-jin irgen-dür kürtele nutuγ darqalan nutuγlažu
sentences.l: Qorchi having-managed, Irtysh-accusative along forest people-to until, camp-ground freely having-camped,
sentences.i: with Qorchi in charge, from the Irtysh as far as the forest peoples, camping freely on their grounds,
sentences.n: medežü 'managing' (mede- 'know' used as 'manage', Ming 管着). Erdis-i is the river (Ming 水名, 'water name') in the accusative -i, and γudus (Ming 緣有) I read as 'along, following': 'along the Irtysh'. hoi-jin irgen-dür kürtele is 'up to the forest people' (hoi 'forest', genitive -jin, Ming 林的; irgen 'people' + dative-locative; kürtele 'until'). nutuγ 'camp-ground, pasture' (Ming 營盤), darqalan 'free, exempt' (Ming 自在), nutuγlažu 'making camp' (the verb from nutuγ + converb -žu). The sense: Qorchi's people are to camp freely in the territory from the Irtysh to the forest peoples.

morph.gloss: the Irtysh, a river (Ming 水名) [水(名)]
along, following (Ming 緣有; uncertain) [緣有]
free, at liberty (Ming 自在) [自在]
to make camp (from nutuγ) [做營盤着]

sentences.t: hoi-jin irgen-i daruγ̇ulun Qorči tümen medetügei" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Forest people-accusative having-caused-to-submit, Qorchi ten-thousand let-him-govern, saying, decree it-was-made.
sentences.i: and subduing the forest peoples. Let Qorchi govern the ten-thousand.” So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: hoi-jin irgen-i is 'the forest people' in the accusative; daruγ̇ulun is a causative converb of daru- 'press down, subdue' (-γ̇ul-, Ming 敎鎭 'cause to be suppressed'). Qorči tümen medetügei is 'let Qorchi govern a ten-thousand' (medetügei as at §205). Shiratori's closing mark is at medetügei", closing the speech opened at Qorči (393). The decree frame again.

morph.gloss: ten-thousand, a division of ten thousand [萬戶]
to become, to be made [做了]

sentences.t: "Qorči-dāča eje ügeiġü hoi-jin irgen ein tein bu jabutuγ̇ai.
sentences.l: Qorchi-from consent without forest people thus thus not let-them-go.
sentences.i: “Without Qorchi's consent, let the forest peoples not go this way or that.
sentences.n: Qorči-dāča is Qorchi + an ending written dāča (long ā is Shiratori's); the Ming give 行 'to', but 'without X's consent' (eje ügeiġü) needs the ablative 'from', so I take -dāča as a lengthened ablative -ača (back-vowel, as the -eče of keġer-eče); the Ming gloss is uncertain. eje is 'consent, counsel' (Ming 商量), ügeiġü 'without'. ein tein is 'this way, that way' (Ming 這般 那般), bu jabutuγ̇ai is 'let (them) not go' (the prohibitive bu 'not', Ming 休, with jabu- and the third-person imperative -tuγ̇ai, Ming 行者︀). Opening quotation mark (Shiratori's) at Qorči-dāča.

morph.gloss: ablative (uncertain; long form of -ača; the Ming read 行): 'from, by' [行]
counsel, consent, leave (Ming 商量) [商量]

sentences.t: Eje ügeġü jabuqu-ji jaγ̇u saγ̇araγdaqu" keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: Consent without going-one-accusative what to-be-doubted? saying, decree it-was-made.
sentences.i: What doubt is there about one who goes without consent?” So he issued the decree.
sentences.n: The rhetorical close: eje ügeġü jabuqu-ji is 'the one going without consent' (jabu- + participle -qu + accusative -ji, Ming 行的每 行); jaγ̇u saγ̇araγdaqu is 'what is there to be doubted?' (saγ̇ara- 'to doubt, hesitate' + the passive -γda- + the future participle -qu; Ming 甚 疑惑). The sense is that there is no hesitation in punishing him, but the Ming give only 'what doubt'. Note ügeiġü / ügeġü, two spellings of the same word in one sentence. Closing mark at saγ̇araγdaqu"; the frame ends the section as at §204–206.

morph.gloss: counsel, consent, leave (Ming 商量) [商量]
to go, to act [行的每 行]
to become, to be made [做了]
